nodes.assumption: The era floor—this ticket's PROVED crossing timestamp—is stored in a location the probe code can read at runtime (such as the ticket's phase_writes array, CairnCommons/tickets/<ticket-id>.json with standing='PROVED'), or accessible via a standard Cairn function.
nodes.would_settle: Specify where and how the probe reads the PROVED crossing timestamp: e.g., 'read it from phase_writes by finding the entry where standing="PROVED", or call a function like get_ticket_proved_time(ticket_id)'.

nodes.assumption: record_delivery(id, to, by) is the bus's method to persist a delivery record into db_domain and receipt the envelope; it exists or the builder creates it calling through db_domain
nodes.would_settle: record_delivery's interface and import path spelled out once in the bus, or a note that it is db_domain's receipting verb

nodes.assumption: The builder can determine whether a mail envelope has an undeclared/uncallable verb or lacks a receive handler by inspecting the envelope against the addressee device's declared verbs and interface; the decision lists the identity names for each case but not the detection logic.
nodes.would_settle: Specify the mechanism to detect whether an envelope's verb is unsupported (undeclared or uncallable) vs whether the addressee has no receive() method at all.

nodes.assumption: The era floor (this ticket's PROVED crossing timestamp) is made available to the probe module at runtime—either as a literal written into the probe file at PROVED time, or read from the ticket's crossing record, or injected by the system. The decision says 'written as a literal at the crossing' but does not specify the mechanism or timing.
nodes.would_settle: Specify whether the era floor is (a) hardcoded into the probe source at PROVED time, (b) read from the ticket's crossing record at runtime, or (c) provided another way, and clarify when this value becomes available.

nodes.assumption: The builder can correctly map the test cases described in D7 to teeth (individual test assertions) and name them in the PROVES block with proper correspondence to the falsifier clauses. The decision specifies what each proof should test ('a sleeping addressee is woken', 'a bounce is not re-sent', etc.) but does not list the tooth names or clarify how they relate to the falsifier's now-dead census clause.
nodes.would_settle: List the tooth names and falsifier clauses that the two proofs should test (or confirm they should be derived from the hypothesize chart's 10 teeth).
